question: Where is the primary definition of domain 0 / RT0, and what did it say?
why_it_matters: RT0 is the region the whole track holds separate, and its naming source - Malik, Burke & Eickbush 1999, where domain Z was renamed domain 0 - is not held by this project. Both held sources that state RT0's scope cite it rather than derive it.
evidence_state_after_g1: Scope verified twice at the PDFs (Zimmerly 2001, Simon 2008); the defining source itself is unheld and unread.
blocking_for: g2 reconstruction of any RT0 landmark; any RT0 correspondence test
default_taken: Treat RT0 as OUT_OF_FRAME outside group II intron and non-LTR RTs, per launcher 7a, and carry the scope statement as a verified prior rather than as a definition.

question: Which blocks do Simon & Zimmerly's 59 across-the-set alignable characters fall in?
why_it_matters: The prior dossier records these 59 characters as lying in RT domains 3-5. That localisation is what would make the number a statement about which blocks transfer, and this track's per-class occupancy matrix is meant to improve on exactly that.
evidence_state_after_g1: The running text states the count (59) and the per-class counts, but nowhere in the extracted text does it place the 59 characters in domains 3-5. The localisation is currently unsupported by the text this gate read.
blocking_for: g6 comparison against the published transferability benchmark
default_taken: Record the count as published and the block localisation as UNVERIFIED; check Figure 4 in g2 or g7 before any use.

question: Do the printed Figure 1 columns of Xiong & Eickbush 1990 yield per-block extents?
why_it_matters: The seven-way partition originates there, and the text gives criteria but no per-block coordinates. Extents exist only as printed alignment columns.
evidence_state_after_g1: Routes 1 and 2 of launcher 5e were checked in this gate. Route 1 fails: the paper cites no accessioned or deposited alignment. Route 2 succeeds for the criteria but yields no coordinates.
default_taken: Do not digitise in g1. Digitisation is now the authorised fallback for extents in g2, under launcher 5e, with extraction uncertainty attached to every pixel-derived edge.

question: Can the numbered subdomains be recovered on ALIGN_000044 by re-deriving them, rather than read off it?
why_it_matters: The acquired primary alignment is the artefact Zimmerly 2001 adjusted its inherited labels against, so it is the closest thing to a ground-truth coordinate system the history offers - but it annotates only three domains.
evidence_state_after_g1: Acquired and verified in this gate: 66 sequences, 1441 columns, RT domain at columns 261-886, zero subdomain annotations detected by a detector validated on the same file.
default_taken: Reconstruct the blocks on the alignment in g2 from the conservation criteria, and report recovery as a measurement; do not assume the labels transfer.

question: Is the manual adjustment step in ALIGN_000044 reproducible?
why_it_matters: The alignment's stated method is PILEUP, CLUSTALX and manual adjustment. The manual step cannot be rerun, so the alignment is a primary artefact but not a reproducible procedure.
evidence_state_after_g1: Stated in the record itself and verified in this gate.
blocking_for: any claim that g2 rebuilt the authors frame exactly
default_taken: Treat ALIGN_000044 as a fixed primary artefact to measure against, never as a procedure to re-execute.

question: Is Blocker's RT0 (M1-R85) boundary transferable beyond LtrA?
why_it_matters: It is the only residue-coordinate RT0 boundary in the held set, and it is attractive precisely because coordinates are scarce.
evidence_state_after_g1: Verified at the PDF: it is a proteolytic fragment boundary on one protein, from a Tier-1 structural source that may not seed the sequence partition.
blocking_for: g4 boundary model; g7 structural comparison
default_taken: Use only as a constraint or falsifier in g7, never as a seed or an acceptance criterion.

question: Does the trap D10 - citing Simon & Zimmerly as licensing a LIV criterion - stay closed?
why_it_matters: A registered trap that was already paid for once. The paper's nearly always hydrophobic statement is about position 2 of Y/FxDD, while the excluded class differs elsewhere.
evidence_state_after_g1: Verified verbatim at the PDF in this gate.
blocking_for: any motif-based eligibility rule in g4
default_taken: Keep the trap in this register so it cannot be re-walked; do not derive a residue-class criterion from that sentence.

question: Is domain 1's weaker support in 1990 the same object as a later RT1 concordance failure?
why_it_matters: The founding authors state that domain 1 alone was not independently confirmed. A modern RT1 concordance failure would be tempting to read as recovering that weakness.
evidence_state_after_g1: Verified at the PDF in this gate. The two objects remain distinct: one is 1990 evidence provenance, the other a 2026 measurement.
blocking_for: g3 prior-method replication; the interpretation of any RT1 result
default_taken: None taken. Interpretation is an operator decision under launcher 9b and decision record section Deliberately deferred; g1 only records that both objects exist and are different.
